evidence.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.
That's because the next interest payment equals 5 percent of $1,050, or $52.50.
So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).
After the first year, you would have $1,050—your original principal, plus 5 percent, or $50.
The second year, you would have $1,102.50.
Interest can be compounded annually (once each year), semi-annually (twice each year), monthly, or daily.

objectives: Understand how time and compound interest can increase savings
Understand the value of starting early to save for post-secondary education
